title: Nested JSON to Delta: struct fields and explode
objective_text: Ingest nested JSON into Delta: schemas, struct access, explode and semi-structured types.
scenario: Sensors post JSON events that Auto Loader lands in bronze.device_events with the schema it inferred: device is a struct holding a site struct, and readings is an array of structs. The operations team wants silver.readings with one row per reading, and a silent-device report that needs every device that sent nothing to still show up. The feed retries, so some events arrive twice.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: A Delta table bronze.device_events (6 rows, nested struct and array columns) in the exercise folder, and a starter answer.py.
required: One row per event_id before flattening: a retried event counts once.
An event with an empty or missing readings array keeps one row, with metric and value NULL.
device_id and site_code come from the device struct (device.id and device.site.code).
Write silver.readings with event_id, device_id, site_code, metric, value, so that running the code again leaves the same table.

expected.description: silver.readings has 8 rows: 2 for event 1, 1 for event 2, 3 for event 4, and one row each with no reading for events 3 and 5.

verifies: Your PySpark reads nested struct fields and flattens an array of structs, keeping events with no readings, on the exercise data and on rows you haven't seen, on this PC.
Running it again leaves the same table.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run Auto Loader or Lakeflow Connect, read raw JSON files or infer a schema: the table starts with the nested schema already inferred.
It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in a Databricks workspace.
hints: events.printSchema() shows the nesting. F.col("device.site.code") reads a field inside a struct inside a struct.
dropDuplicates(["event_id"]) before flattening keeps a retried event from doubling its readings.
F.explode drops a row whose array is empty or NULL. F.explode_outer keeps it once, with the element NULL.
Write with mode("overwrite") so a rerun replaces the table.
explanation: Drop duplicate event_ids first, because a retried event would otherwise double every one of its readings. Then explode_outer the readings array: it gives one row per element and, unlike explode, keeps one row with NULLs for an empty or missing array, which is what the silent-device report needs. Read device.id and device.site.code with dot paths, take metric and value from the reading struct, and overwrite silver.readings so a rerun can't double it.
troubleshooting: Events 3 and 5 are missing: explode drops empty and NULL arrays; use explode_outer.
Event 2's reading appears twice: drop duplicate event_ids before flattening.
Event 4 has one row, not three: readings[0] reads only the first element; explode the array.
site_code shows GB or FR: that's device.site.country; the code is device.site.code.
reset: Reset rebuilds bronze.device_events from setup.sql, removes silver.readings and puts the starter back.
cleanup: Everything lives in this exercise's folder on this PC; Reset or removing the exercise deletes it. Nothing is created in any workspace.
